aboutPage.title: Print It Yourself
aboutPage.introBody: 3DPIY started from a simple idea: if you own a 3D printer, you shouldn't have to settle for generic files. Every design here is modeled from scratch, test-printed, and refined before it's released — practical objects you'll actually use, not just things that look good in a render.
aboutPage.makerBody: 3DPIY is a one-person studio. I design, test-print and document every file myself before it goes live — from a quick IKEA fix to a full dollhouse miniature. I care about things that actually work on your printer, with clear instructions and no guesswork.
values: Designed and tested in-house — nothing published without a real test print
Clear, honest documentation — materials, settings and limitations, no surprises
Independent and small on purpose — direct contact, no faceless support queue

calculatorPage.title: 3D print cost & price calculator
calculatorPage.metaDescription: Free 3D print cost calculator: filament, electricity, your time, platform fees and VAT — and the price to sell your 3D prints for on Etsy or your own shop.
calculatorPage.intro: What does a 3D print really cost, and what should you ask for it? Fill in filament, print time and your time — the calculator gives the cost price and a selling price that still leaves you a profit after platform fees and VAT.
calculatorPage.howBody: First the cost price per item: filament (grams × price per kg), electricity (power × print time × kWh price), printer wear, failed prints and your own time. Then the selling price is calculated backwards, so that what's left after VAT and platform fees is exactly the profit you want.
calculatorPage.formula: price = (cost price + fixed fees + profit) ÷ ((1 − margin) ÷ (1 + VAT) − platform %)
calculatorPage.howBody2: Selling on Etsy? Etsy charges a transaction fee, payment processing and a listing fee on every sale — choose Etsy and they're included. Prices are rounded up to .99 by default.

q1.q: How much does it cost to 3D print something?
q1.a: For a typical PLA print the filament is often only €0.50–€3; electricity is a few cents per hour. The real costs are your time, failed prints, printer wear, packaging and platform fees — which is why the cost price is usually several times the filament cost.

q2.q: How do I calculate the price to sell a 3D print for?
q2.a: Add up the cost price per item (filament, electricity, wear, failed prints, your time, extras and packaging), choose the profit you want, and work back from VAT and platform fees. This calculator does that for you.

q3.q: What does Etsy charge per sale?
q3.a: In the Netherlands roughly 6.5% transaction fee plus about 4% + €0.30 payment processing, and a listing fee of about €0.19 per sale; Offsite Ads can add up to 15%. Fees change, so check Etsy's current rates.

q4.q: Do I have to charge VAT on 3D prints?
q4.a: In the Netherlands you charge 21% VAT unless you use the small business scheme (KOR, up to €20,000 turnover a year). Choose the option that applies to you; this is not tax advice.

q5.q: How much electricity does a 3D printer use?
q5.a: A Bambu Lab P1S or X1 uses about 100–150 W on average while printing — at €0.30 per kWh that's roughly 3–5 cents per print hour.

q6.q: May I sell prints of designs I downloaded?
q6.a: Only if the license allows it. Most free and personal licenses don't. 3DPIY Business sells commercial licenses that let you sell physical prints.
